It was great connecting with you at NASCC 2026 in Atlanta. I hope the conference was as productive for you as it was for us, and that the conversations it sparked continue to open doors.

Pick one of your current or recent projects and we will run it through our full intelligence system at no cost.

The platform is built on two years of structured research, every claim below is sourced and linked on our site under [Research Transparency].

You will receive four reports:

  • 268 documented pain points across 5 dimensions (frequency, severity, cost consequence, strategic importance, stakeholder breadth).
  • 1,266 risks mapped across 5 project stages. Shop drawing cycle risk scores 72/100, the #1 risk in the registry, and drives 35 to 45% of all field changes.
  • 99 verified case studies with measured outcomes, matched to your specific pain profile.
  • 332 operational templates, 64% AI-automatable (214 agents). We tell you exactly which ones works for you.

For structural engineers specifically, we cross-check the three documents where the design intent either holds up under fabrication and field reality or gets quietly rewritten by everyone downstream:

Design Drawings & Specifications line-by-line, for completeness, AISC code reference clarity, BIM LOD compliance, and scope-of-work allocation between the EOR and the detailing chain. Contract documents are 50 to 70% complete on average when they go out to bid (R-1.2-002, scored 56/100 in the risk registry); BIM models delivered at LOD 300 routinely get pushed back because fabrication needs LOD 400 to 500 (R-1.4-015). We flag exactly where your drawings are leaving the next reviewer, fabricator, detailer, or contractor to guess.

Connection Design & Delegated Design Package connection design responsibility is the single most disputed scope item in steel projects, scored 64/100 in the risk registry (R-1.2-005), with EOR and fabricator each assuming the other owns it. We map exactly which connections are EOR-designed, which are delegated under AISC CoSP §4, which calculations belong to whom, and where the delegated-design submittal is most likely to bounce on first approval.

Shop Drawing Review Cycle your review burden, benchmarked against 99 documented projects, predicted RFI density, turnaround time, and the change-order exposure that flows from review delays. Shop drawing cycle risk is the #1 risk in the registry at 72/100, and 35 to 45% of all field changes originate in this cycle. The industry captures 96% of its project data and analyzes almost none of it (FMI Corp, PP-TH-002) we wire historical feedback into one cycle, free, so you can see the delta.

What a structural engineer walks away with:

  • A documented design package readiness audit LOD gaps, missing dimensions, ambiguous notes, AISC code reference inconsistencies, and scope-allocation conflicts flagged before they become RFIs.
  • A connection design responsibility map every connection tagged as EOR-designed, delegated, or undefined, with the calculation-package gaps that will hold up approval and the AISC CoSP §4 compliance checklist applied.
  • A shop drawing review workload forecast your predicted RFI volume, review cycle time, and reviewer-hour exposure benchmarked against 99 real projects of similar scope and complexity.
  • A BIM LOD handoff readiness report where your model is sitting at LOD 300 vs. the LOD 400 to 500 fabrication needs, and which specific elements are likely to drive coordination RFIs.
  • A delegated-design specification template you can reuse on the next ten projects.

The diagnosis surfaces exactly where the design-to-construction exposure sits on your current project, against two years of research, at no cost to you.
If it earns a conversation, we'll talk. If not, you keep the report.

I'll personally make sure your four reports are back in your inbox shortly.

The part most researchers ask about first: the methodology.
The five-step research protocol is published, you can read it, critique it, or use it as the basis for a methodology paper of your own.
If you find a flaw, we want to hear about it. That is the contract of open research.

Three concrete ways the dataset can support your work:

1. Validation query a slice of the corpus filtered to your research area and stress-test our scoring against your own analysis. We will send the slice in machine-readable format (CSV / JSON) with full citations attached.

2. Expansion if your dissertation or paper is filling a gap we have already identified (and there are many), we can co-validate findings, share data lineage, and discuss formal acknowledgment or co-authorship.

3. Citation the corpus has a stable reference. If you cite it in a publication, conference paper, or thesis, the reference format is on page.

What a researcher walks away with:

  • A filtered corpus slice built around your topic, pain points, risks, and case studies tagged to your research domain.
  • A methodology brief, the five-step protocol, the source taxonomy, the scoring rubric, the normalization rules, open for review and critique.
  • A citation reference ready to drop into your bibliography.
  • A short call with Prof. Dr. Neo Ekici to discuss research fit, validation pathways, and potential publication routes.
    (Research Director, xPM Solutions)

We do not believe industry data should be locked behind sales gates from the researchers building the next decade of this field.
If your research touches structural steel, project delivery, AI in construction, risk analysis, BIM, or workforce, this dataset supports your research.

Reply with one line, your research topic, or the slice you want, and we will route it to you shortly.

We model your steel critical path against 99 documented projects and flag every node where schedule certainty is sitting on a contingency rather than a control.
